objective: By the end of this lesson you can make standard rate turns to assigned headings using only the flight instruments, holding altitude and airspeed and rolling out on the heading within ACS limits.
why: Turning is where pilots without the horizon get into trouble: overbanking can become a graveyard spiral. A calm, standard rate turn to a heading lets you follow ATC vectors back to clear air.

warmup: You are told to turn from heading 030° to 120°. Which way do you turn, how steep do you bank, and when do you start the roll-out?

key_terms.def: A turn of 3° per second: a full 360° in 2 minutes.
Rate gyro tilted about 30° so it shows roll rate first, then rate of turn. Gives no pitch information.
Shows if the turn is coordinated. Ball to the outside = skid; ball to the inside = slip.
Starting the roll-out before the heading, about half the bank angle in degrees.
A turn using the clock and turn coordinator instead of the heading indicator.
Gyro drift or error, such as the heading indicator drifting or the attitude indicator showing a small error after a turn.
A descending turn the pilot can't feel; pulling back only tightens it.

chunks.title: The bank instruments and what they show

body.p: Bank instruments are the attitude indicator, heading indicator, magnetic compass and turn coordinator or turn-and-slip indicator [[23:140|IFH 6-7]]. Only the attitude indicator shows actual attitude directly and at once [[23:140|IFH 6-7]].

head: Instrument
How it works
Use in a turn
rows: Gyro stays upright while the airplane rolls around it; bank scale marks 10°, 20°, 30°, 45°, 60° [[23:114|IFH 5-19]]
Set the bank angle on roll-in; primary bank during roll-out [[23:181|IFH 7-20]]
Rate gyro tilted about 30°, so it senses roll and yaw. Shows rate of roll first, then rate of turn [[23:116|IFH 5-21]]. No pitch information [[23:117|IFH 5-22]]
Primary bank once the turn is set: hold the wing on the standard rate mark [[23:181|IFH 7-20]]
Senses yaw only. Needle on the 'doghouse' of a 2 MIN instrument = standard rate [[23:116|IFH 5-21]]
Centered = coordinated. Outside of turn = skid. Inside of turn = slip [[23:116|IFH 5-21]] [[23:117|IFH 5-22]]
Check it all through the turn [[23:181|IFH 7-20]]
Gyro with a horizontal spin axis; not north-seeking, set it from the compass [[23:115|IFH 5-20]]
Shows where you are in the turn and when to roll out; primary bank once wings are level [[23:181|IFH 7-20]]
Altimeter is primary for pitch; airspeed is primary for power in a constant airspeed turn [[23:181|IFH 7-20]]

body.p: On a glass panel, the turn rate indicator sits on the compass rose [[23:213|IFH 7-52]]. It is the only instrument that can show a standard rate turn exactly, so it is primary for bank in the turn [[23:212|IFH 7-51]].

check.q: Why can't the turn coordinator show if your nose is high or low?
check.a: It senses only roll and yaw, not pitch. Some are marked 'NO PITCH INFORMATION' [[23:117|IFH 5-22]].

chunks.title: Instrument limits and errors in turns

head: Instrument
Limitation or error
rows: Small bank and pitch error possible after a 180° turn; it corrects within a minute or so after level flight [[23:114|IFH 5-19]]
Drifts about 15° per hour because the earth turns. Check against the compass at least every 15 minutes [[23:115|IFH 5-20]]
Steeper than about 18° of bank, readings are erratic [[23:106|IFH 5-11]]. Leads and lags in turns [[23:140|IFH 6-7]]
May not be exact. Calibrate it: a true standard rate turn changes heading 30° in 10 seconds [[23:182|IFH 7-21]]
With no roll rate, it shows only direction and rate of turn. Don't assume a bank unless the ball is centered [[23:187|IFH 7-26]]

callout.text: After a roll-out, if the attitude indicator shows wings level but the heading keeps changing: ball centered = the attitude gyro has precessed; ball not centered = you're slipping or skidding. Center the ball, stop the turn, retrim [[23:186|IFH 7-25]].

check.q: How do you check whether your turn coordinator's standard rate mark is accurate?
check.a: Hold the standard rate indication and note the heading every 10 seconds. A true standard rate turn changes 30° in 10 seconds; if not, note the corrected deflection and use it [[23:182|IFH 7-21]].

body.p: In the inverted-V cross-check, look from the attitude indicator down to the turn coordinator, back up, down to the VSI, and back up [[23:144|IFH 6-11]]. It fits turns well: bank on one side, pitch on the other.

bullets: Roll-in: check pitch instruments as soon as bank pressure starts. Lift goes down as bank goes up [[23:186|IFH 7-25]].
During a 90° turn at standard rate, you can leave the heading indicator out for about 20 seconds; you won't reach the lead point before then [[23:186|IFH 7-25]].
Make the cross-check selective: check what needs checking at that moment [[23:186|IFH 7-25]].
Fixation on the turn rate indicator is a major error. A modified radial scan works well [[23:213|IFH 7-52]].
After the roll-out, keep the straight-and-level cross-check going. Errors often follow a perfect turn [[23:186|IFH 7-25]].

check.q: In a 90° standard rate turn, why is staring at the heading indicator wasted effort?
check.a: At 3° per second it takes about 20 seconds to near the lead point, so check pitch and bank instead [[23:186|IFH 7-25]].

chunks.title: Bank angle, direction and roll-out lead

head: Question
Rule
Example
rows: Turn the shortest way unless you have a reason not to [[23:186|IFH 7-25]]
305° to 110°: reciprocal of 305 = 305 − 200 + 20 = 125, so 110 is to the right [[23:186|IFH 7-25]]
About 15% of true airspeed: airspeed ÷ 10, plus half that [[23:180|IFH 7-19]] [[23:181|IFH 7-20]]
Bank no more than the degrees to turn [[23:181|IFH 7-20]]. Glass section: about half the heading change, never more than standard rate [[23:213|IFH 7-52]]
Lead by half the bank angle [[23:181|IFH 7-20]]
030° to 120° with 15° bank: roll out at about 112° [[23:214|IFH 7-53]]

callout.text: Bank = speed ÷ 10 + half. Lead = half the bank. Same roll-in and roll-out rate [[23:181|IFH 7-20]].

body.p: No heading indicator? Do a timed turn: start the roll-in as the second hand passes a cardinal point, hold standard rate, and roll out when the computed seconds are up [[23:182|IFH 7-21]].

check.q: At 90 knots, about what bank gives a standard rate turn?

body.p: The IFH method for a level standard rate turn at constant airspeed [[23:180|IFH 7-19]] [[23:181|IFH 7-20]]:

bullets: 1. Find the direction, the bank angle and the roll-out heading (half the bank before the target).
2. Roll in with coordinated aileron and rudder. Don't roll faster than you can cross-check [[23:180|IFH 7-19]].
3. Set the approximate bank on the attitude indicator, then check the turn coordinator for standard rate. Hold it with the turn coordinator as primary bank [[23:181|IFH 7-20]].
4. As bank increases, check altimeter, VSI and attitude indicator. Add a little back pressure to hold altitude [[23:181|IFH 7-20]].
5. Add power as drag increases to hold airspeed. Trim off the pressures [[23:181|IFH 7-20]].
6. At the lead point, roll out at the same rate you rolled in [[23:181|IFH 7-20]].
7. Lower the nose as bank decreases so you don't climb [[23:212|IFH 7-51]]. Release back pressure and take out the power you added [[23:185|IFH 7-24]].
8. Wings level: heading indicator is primary bank again. Trim, and keep the scan going [[23:181|IFH 7-20]].

callout.text: These limits are from ACS PA.VIII.D.S1. Aim for zero error.

check.q: During the roll-in, which instrument is primary for bank, and which takes over once the turn is set?
check.a: Attitude indicator first to set the bank; then the turn coordinator for standard rate [[23:181|IFH 7-20]].

body.p: From the IFH list of common errors in turns [[23:186|IFH 7-25]] [[23:187|IFH 7-26]]:

head: Area
Error
Result or fix
rows: Busy with bank on entry; forgetting lift drops in a bank
Altitude loss on entry. Check pitch as bank starts
Not lowering the nose on roll-out
Pulling back before it is needed, or too much
Overcontrolled pitch. Pull only as the altimeter and VSI show a need
Too much bank for a small change, e.g. 20° bank for 10°
Overshoot. Bank no more than the change
Forgetting the target heading or turning the wrong way
Say the heading and direction out loud
Not checking airspeed as pitch changes; chasing airspeed
Not trimming after entry or power changes
Tension on controls; hard to sense pressures

callout.text: Overbanking with low pitch: altimeter and VSI dropping fast and airspeed rising, even with back pressure, means a diving spiral. Shallow the bank first, then raise the nose. Reduce power if speed builds fast [[23:184|IFH 7-23]].

check.q: You keep losing altitude on every turn entry. Most likely cause?
check.a: Not adding back pressure as the vertical lift component drops, often from being busy with bank [[23:186|IFH 7-25]].

chunks.title: Risk: disorientation, help, traffic and distraction

body.p: The inner ear takes about 15 to 20 seconds to catch up in a turn [[23:71|IFH 3-4]]. In a steady turn you feel no turn. When you roll out, you feel a turn the other way and may roll back in [[23:72|IFH 3-5]].

head: Hazard
What to do
rows: In a long turn you lose altitude but feel level. Pulling back tightens the spiral [[23:73|IFH 3-6]]. Trust the instruments; level the wings first
After a slow roll-in and quick correction you feel banked the other way. Fly the attitude indicator [[23:72|IFH 3-5]]
Moving your head in a long turn can cause strong false sensations. Keep head movement small [[23:73|IFH 3-6]]
Turns are the most dangerous maneuver for the untrained. Use no more than 10° bank; turn a few degrees, level, repeat [[24:368|AFH 18-19]]

Ask for help the moment you doubt position, fuel, weather or safety [[34:28|AIM 6-1-2]]. Not instrument rated and can't stay VFR: tell ATC and declare a distress condition [[34:29|AIM 6-2-1]]. Squawk 7700 [[34:29|AIM 6-2-2]]
Don't let ATC urgency rush a turn; ask them to slow down [[24:370|AFH 18-21]]

The safety pilot must hold at least a private pilot certificate with the right category and class ratings [[60:446|14 CFR 91.109(c)(1)]], and have a good view forward and to each side, or a competent observer to help [[60:447|14 CFR 91.109(c)(2)]]. Safety pilots tend to look inside too much [[16:15|AC 90-48E 17.2]]

Fatigue hurts attention and coordination; with acute fatigue, stay on the ground [[1:435|PHAK 17-13]]. Chronic stress makes performance fall off fast; a pilot under that much stress should not fly [[1:434|PHAK 17-12]]. In the air, reduce your workload and stay calm: think, weigh the options, then act [[9:21|AC 60-22 par 21e]]
If weather traps you, a precautionary landing while you still have options beats a forced landing later [[24:350|AFH 18-1]]

check.q: After a long turn you roll out and feel like you're turning the other way. What do you do?
check.a: Believe the instruments and keep the wings level. The feeling is from inner-ear fluid, not real motion [[23:72|IFH 3-5]] [[24:367|AFH 18-18]].

scenario.title: Vectors in the haze
scenario.setup: You and your CFI are on a practice flight at 4,500 ft, 100 knots, when the horizon disappears in haze. Approach gives you a vector: 'turn right heading 120'. You are on 030°. Your CFI sits back and says, 'Fly it.' A few minutes later the controller quickly calls another turn, 'turn left heading 090, expedite.' You notice you feel a little dizzy.

questions.q: How do you fly the first turn?
questions.a: Right turn, standard rate: about 15° bank at 100 knots [[23:181|IFH 7-20]]. Roll out about half the bank early, around 112° [[23:214|IFH 7-53]]. It takes about 30 seconds (90° at 3° per second) [[23:180|IFH 7-19]].

questions.q: The controller sounds rushed. Do you crank in a steep bank?
questions.a: No. Don't let ATC urgency push you into a maneuver you can't control; it's fine to ask them to slow down [[24:370|AFH 18-21]].

questions.q: You feel dizzy after rolling out of the turn. What is happening and what do you do?
questions.a: Likely a vestibular illusion after the turn [[23:72|IFH 3-5]]. Trust the attitude indicator, keep the wings level and keep head movement small [[23:73|IFH 3-6]] [[24:367|AFH 18-18]].

questions.q: If this happened solo and you couldn't stay VFR, what should you tell ATC?
questions.a: That you are not instrument rated, and declare a distress condition [[34:29|AIM 6-2-1]].

questions.q: Who watches for traffic while you're on instruments in training?
questions.a: The safety pilot or CFI, who must have a good view out [[60:447|14 CFR 91.109(c)(2)]] and must not get stuck looking inside [[16:15|AC 90-48E 17.2]].

skills.do: Turn to assigned headings at standard rate, holding altitude ±200 ft and airspeed ±10 knots, and roll out on heading ±10° (ACS PA.VIII.D.S1).
skills.practice: Under the hood with a safety pilot, have them call random headings. Say the direction, bank angle and roll-out heading out loud before each turn [[23:181|IFH 7-20]]. Calibrate the turn coordinator first (30° in 10 seconds) [[23:182|IFH 7-21]], and practice timed turns as a backup [[23:182|IFH 7-21]].

quiz.q: About what bank gives a standard rate turn at 120 knots?
Using 15° of bank to turn to 120°, start the roll-out at about:
Once a standard rate turn is set, which instrument is primary for bank?
quiz.why: The turn coordinator's miniature airplane is primary for bank; the attitude indicator supports it [[23:181|IFH 7-20]].

quiz.q: In a level turn at constant airspeed, the primary pitch instrument is the:
quiz.why: Altimeter is primary for pitch; airspeed is primary for power [[23:181|IFH 7-20]] [[23:214|IFH 7-53]].

quiz.q: In a turn, the ball moves to the outside of the turn. You are:
quiz.why: Ball to the outside = skid; to the inside = slip [[23:116|IFH 5-21]] [[23:117|IFH 5-22]].

quiz.q: To turn from 305° to 110° the shortest way, you turn:
quiz.why: Reciprocal of 305 is 125, so 110 is to the right [[23:186|IFH 7-25]].

quiz.q: ACS limits for turns to headings include roll-out heading within:
quiz.why: ACS PA.VIII.D.S1: roll out on heading ±10°, altitude ±200 ft, airspeed ±10 knots, standard rate.

takeaways: Standard rate = 3° per second. Bank ≈ airspeed ÷ 10 + half.
Turn the shortest way; roll out early by half the bank.
Attitude indicator sets the bank; turn coordinator holds standard rate; altimeter holds pitch; airspeed sets power.
Add back pressure and power on roll-in; release them on roll-out; trim.
Check the ball, keep the scan moving, don't fixate on the heading indicator.
Can't feel the turn? Trust the instruments; level the wings and ask for help early.
cfi_notes: The IFH says to leave the heading indicator out of the cross-check for about 20 seconds in a 90° turn (7-25) and about 25 seconds in another place (6-13). The point is the same: don't stare at it.
The IFH gives two small-turn bank rules: no more than the degrees to turn (7-20) and about half the degrees (7-52). Teach the half rule for precision and the 'no more than' rule as a limit.
Common student mistakes: rolling in too fast, losing altitude on entry and gaining it on roll-out. Have them say 'bank, back pressure, power, trim' on entry and the reverse on roll-out.

Calibrate the turn coordinator in the training airplane before timed turns (30° in 10 seconds). The IFH wording on which way to adjust ('respectively larger or smaller deflection', 7-21) is easy to misread; check the result against the heading indicator rather than relying on the wording.
Have the student call each heading, direction and lead out loud; examiners notice wrong-direction turns right away.
Keep your own eyes outside during hood work (AC 90-48E 17.2).
gaps: Power setting changes needed to hold airspeed in a turn are airplane-specific (POH); the IFH only says to add power as drag increases.
The AFH has no turn-to-heading procedure by instruments; it points to the IFH. The step-by-step is from IFH Ch 7.
Stress is covered in general terms (PHAK 17-12, AC 60-22 par 21e); no source here gives a stress-management method specific to instrument flying.
No source gives specific guidance on emergency off-airport landings while in IMC; the AFH covers precautionary vs forced landings in general.
